extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: A bilingual, multitask benchmark for long-context understanding comprising 21 datasets across six task categories: single-document question answering, multi-document question answering, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. It contains 4,750 test instances in English and Chinese, with average lengths of 6,711 English words and 13,386 Chinese characters. LongBench-E is a related evaluation collection with more evenly distributed context lengths across 13 English datasets.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.inLanguage: English; Chinese; code in Python, C#, and Java
extraction.citeAs: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, and Juanzi Li. LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding. arXiv:2308.14508v2 [cs.CL], 19 June 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Six component datasets were extracted directly from existing datasets, ten were adapted from existing datasets for long-context evaluation, and five were created and annotated by the authors. Existing sources were sampled for question answering, summarization, few-shot learning, and code completion. MultiFieldQA was manually curated from documents and articles across multiple fields. Synthetic tasks were constructed from sampled Wikipedia and Chinese C4 passages. Data were extracted from public dataset test sets to reduce test leakage, except VCSUM because its test set had insufficient data. Random sampling produced LongBench with a natural length distribution; length-based uniform sampling produced LongBench-E.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Document analysis; Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing datasets: NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, VCSUM, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, Long Code Completion, and RepoBench-P. Context sources include literature and film scripts, scientific papers, Wikipedia, Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao, U.S. Government Accountability Office and Congressional Research Service reports, meeting transcripts, news articles, dialogues, and GitHub code repositories. MultiFieldQA document sources include arXiv, C4, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, and the Chinese Government Website. Synthetic passage tasks use English Wikipedia and the Chinese sections of C4.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For English multi-document QA, supporting and distracting paragraphs were expanded into complete Wikipedia passages; supporting passages were included first, distracting passages were added up to a maximum context length, and passage order was randomized. DuReader questions were associated with 20 documents, including related documents and randomly selected distractors. MultiNews articles were prefixed with 'Document i' and concatenated. Few-shot contexts were constructed by randomly sampling and concatenating training examples, using example-count ranges of 100–600 for TREC, 10–40 for LSHT, 10–100 for SAMSum, and 2–24 for TriviaQA. PassageRetrieval instances contain 30 randomly sampled passages and a GPT-3.5-Turbo-generated summary of one passage. PassageCount instances were generated by selecting an upper passage count M from 17–50, selecting N unique passages from 2–M, sampling M passages with replacement from those N passages, and shuffling them. RepoBench-P cross-file snippets, including the gold snippet, were shuffled and combined into the context.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 21 datasets were standardized into a unified input, context, and answer format. Single-document QA focused on longer documents, VCSUM used long segments, and TriviaQA example passages were filtered to those with fewer than 1,000 words. RepoBench-P used the Cross-File-First setting, where the in-file context provides no prior usage of the imported module. LongBench-E used word-count-based sampling to obtain comparable quantities of instances in the 0–4k, 4k–8k, and 8k+ length ranges across 13 English datasets. During model evaluation, inputs exceeding a model's maximum context length were truncated from the middle, preserving the beginning and end.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA, three Ph.D. students were invited to create questions and answers for collected articles. Guidelines requested one question and ground-truth answer per document, clear questions with definitive and relatively short answers, evidence distributed as randomly as possible throughout the document, and varied question types including information extraction, summarization, and multi-hop reasoning. Answers were required to be inferable from the documents. Annotation took approximately five minutes per sample. Existing component datasets supplied original question-answer pairs, class labels, summaries, and code-completion targets. Qasper was annotated by NLP practitioners; HotpotQA questions were written by native speakers; MuSiQue questions were paraphrased by annotators; GovReport, MultiNews, and SAMSum provided human-written or human-annotated summaries. PassageRetrieval summaries were generated using GPT-3.5-Turbo, while the answer identifies the corresponding source passage. PassageCount answers are the number of unique passages. Code-completion answers are the next line of code; RepoBench-P includes a manually annotated gold cross-file snippet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among MultiFieldQA annotators showed a reported 100% accuracy rate for annotated answers. MultiFieldQA questions were designed to have definitive, relatively short answers to facilitate automated evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: MultiFieldQA annotators were three Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in NLP, described as expert annotators. Original Qasper annotators were NLP practitioners, and original HotpotQA question writers were native speakers.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo, used to generate summaries for PassageRetrieval-en and PassageRetrieval-zh.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors sought to avoid positional evidence bias in MultiFieldQA by distributing answer evidence randomly rather than concentrating it at the beginning or end of documents. They also identify potential pretraining contamination: models may have encountered source contexts and answer through memorization rather than context understanding. Context-free performance was relatively high on Wikipedia-derived HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue. Test-set extraction was used to reduce leakage, with VCSUM as an exception.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automatic metrics such as ROUGE-L and F1 may not accurately reflect response quality and may underestimate models that generate longer responses. Benchmark performance is coupled with instruction-following ability rather than isolating long-context modeling alone. Summarization and code-completion similarity metrics may insufficiently distinguish strong and weak models. More discriminating synthetic tasks can dominate an aggregate ranking, so the authors caution against treating a simple average over all tasks as the sole indicator of long-context capability. Potential memorization of source material can also confound evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking LLM long-context understanding across single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot in-context learning, synthetic passage retrieval and counting, and code completion. LongBench evaluates overall multitask performance with naturally distributed context lengths; LongBench-E evaluates performance changes across context-length ranges within tasks. The benchmark also supports research on retrieval-based and summarization-based context compression and on distinguishing context understanding from memorization. Evaluation is zero-shot except for tasks with supplied few-shot examples. Automatic metrics include F1, ROUGE-L, classification accuracy, exact-match accuracy, and edit similarity. The authors recommend assessing task categories separately rather than relying only on a simple overall average.
